items.impact: Implementations can disagree on optionality, timestamp naming, blocked/remediation identity fields, score-breakdown structure, capacity-summary shape, and the exact graph-lock transition while still satisfying field-name-only checks.

evidence.exact_quote: - "safe_point_id and remediation lineage are present when relevant."
- "Recovery flow must not silently substitute the main project root or a different worktree when captured worktree context no longer matches."

items.impact: Races between worktree mutation and restore, ambiguous terminal completion, and inconsistent decisions about when lineage or denial mappings are relevant can yield divergent recovery behavior and non-falsifiable implementations.
items.statement: The contract repeatedly uses conditional phrases such as when relevant without a per-event presence matrix, and it does not define atomic snapshot validation, terminal-state enums, retry metadata shape, or conflict behavior when canonical and legacy aliases coexist.

evidence.exact_quote: - "offline_cached is not a blocked_reason_code."

items.impact: Consumers have canonical enum families and are prevented from conflating offline projection state, timeout cause, failure classification, blocked identity, or persisted slash-command shorthand.
items.statement: The window preserves canonical alias precedence and distinct failure, blocked, timeout, wait, offline-cache, and allowed-action identities.
items.title: Runtime taxonomy separations are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - "/abort resolves to abort_run or provider-specific stream cancellation for in-progress provider calls."
- "Future timestamp waits do not produce stall banners or auto-pause until the governing timer actually expires."

items.impact: A destructive shorthand can resolve differently across clients, and clock or timer races can produce inconsistent timeout, wait, auto-pause, and recovery transitions.
items.statement: The contract does not specify the deterministic rule choosing abort_run versus provider cancellation, confirmation and idempotency behavior, timer clock source, expiry transition ordering, or forward-compatible handling of unknown enum values.
items.title: Abort and timer transitions lack deterministic oracles
